smells.finding: estimate_driver_utility is ~40 lines with a single groupby loop; the surrounding logic is already split into 4 small helpers (_valid_mask, _axis_reference_values, _pool_group, _n_points_total). No method exceeds a reasonable length.
No classes defined; the module is pure functions plus one I/O function (write_driver_utility_db).

Checked against sibling driver_utility_observable.py (G1): G1's _validate_inputs/_deficit_and_sem operate on raw telemetry arrays (distance/curvature/v_real/v_ideal); G2's _valid_mask/_pool_group operate on already-pooled per-session rows (g_deficit/sigma_lapsampling) -- different domains, no shared logic duplicated. pool_random_effects and effective_axis_sigma are reused by import, not copy-pasted.

estimate_driver_utility calls pool_random_effects and effective_axis_sigma with well-formed scalar/array arguments; it does not reach into either seam's internal state or fields beyond the documented return (PooledParameter.mu/sigma_mu/tau).

The (year, driver, constructor, axis) grouping tuple recurs but is captured once as the named module constant _GROUP_KEYS and referenced from that single definition throughout the file -- not scattered as repeated inline literals.

status is a plain str ('resolved'/'unresolved'), matching the established seam convention (normalize_axis_status/effective_axis_sigma in estimate_store_fields.py already use plain str status) -- consistent with the codebase's own precedent, not a new primitive-obsession introduction.
estimate_driver_utility(rows_df) takes 1 param; write_driver_utility_db(df, path) takes 2; internal helpers take 1-2 params each. No function approaches a long parameter list.
This is a new, isolated module; no existing caller had to be touched to add it (git diff --stat confirms zero modification outside the 2 new files).
The module has one reason to change (the driver-utility pooling/status/artifact contract); it does not mix unrelated responsibilities.
The one non-trivial chain, sub_all.loc[valid.loc[sub_all.index]], is a standard pandas boolean-mask-alignment idiom (2 hops), not an object navigation chain reaching through unrelated layers.

No unused hooks, abstract base classes, or generality beyond what the close criteria require; MIN_RESOLVED_SESSIONS/REFERENCE_VALUE_FLOOR_MS are concrete tunable constants actually used, not speculative extension points.

The one substantial inline comment block (lines 171-181, explaining the value=None-for-unresolved choice) documents a genuinely subtle, independently-confirmed trap in the REUSED effective_axis_sigma seam (value beats reference_value whenever value is not None) -- it explains a non-obvious cross-module precedence rule, not a workaround for locally confusing code. The code itself (a single conditional expression) is already clear without the comment; the comment adds seam-level context a reader could not get from this file alone.
